This allows proving that conditional probabilities of events E in product spaces converge to either 0 or 1 depending on whether the point belongs to E or its complement. The proof leverages the existence of cylinder sets approximating E within prescribed error bounds, enabling control over measure differences. Specifically, given any δ < 1, one constructs a measurable cylinder E₀ such that μ(E Δ E₀) < ε, defining B = E Δ E₀. Then, sets Cₙ capture points where distance from B under transformation Tₙ exceeds δ, and Dₙ isolates new contributions beyond previous Cᵢ. These constructions ensure convergence properties hold except possibly on negligible sets. The key insight is that these approximations allow for rigorous handling of infinite-dimensional product spaces while maintaining tractable measure-theoretic arguments.
